cues.text: Introduction: Today's Idea
Different countries and travel places can feel like different moods.
Some places feel quiet and organized.
Some places feel lively and modern.
Some places feel natural, friendly, historic, warm, or easy to use.
Today, do not start by choosing a country.
Start with your personality.
First, describe what kind of trip feels good for you.
Then choose a travel style.
After that, compare a few country matches.
At the end, build your result sentence and suggest a place for a friend.
This is not real travel advice.
It is a speaking activity.
Before a real trip, always check the season, budget, rules, and safety.
Start With Your Travel Mood.
A good trip is not only about famous places.
It is also about the feeling you want.
Some people want calm.
Some people want excitement.
Some people want nature, food, culture, comfort, or easy English practice.
What feeling do you want on a trip?
Starter: On a trip, I want to feel because.
Do you want to feel relaxed or active?
Do you want quiet time or many things to do?
What feeling do you not want on a trip?
Would your answer change if you travelled with family?
Helpful expressions: I want to feel calm.
I want to feel excited.
I want something easy and comfortable.
I do not want to feel stressed.
Start With Your Travel Mood.
Imagine you have one free afternoon in a new place.
Choose the option that feels best today.
A. Sit in a quiet cafe and look at a nice view.
B. Walk through a lively city with shops and lights.
C. Go outside to see mountains, water, or open sky.
D. Visit an old street, museum, castle, or market.
E. Eat local food and take beautiful photos.
On a free afternoon, what would you choose?
Starter: I would choose because.
Which option sounds relaxing?
Which option sounds tiring?
Which option would be fun for only one day?
Which option fits your normal personality?
Helpful expressions: That sounds like my style.
That sounds nice, but maybe too busy.
I could enjoy that for one day.
I usually prefer.
Start With Your Travel Mood.
A place can look beautiful online, but still be wrong for your real life.
Think about budget, weather, crowds, transport, food, language, safety, and comfort.
What can ruin a trip for you?
Starter: A trip is difficult for me when.
Is budget very important for you?
Do you dislike very hot or very cold weather?
Do crowded places make you tired?
Do you need easy transport or English support?
Helpful expressions: I need a simple plan.
I do not want to spend too much.
Very hot weather is difficult for me.
I need easy transport.
Build Your Travel Profile.
Choose the letter that is closest to you today.
You can change your answer later.
A. Calm Planner: quiet, organized, comfortable, scenic.
B. City Explorer: modern, lively, easy to move around.
C. Nature Recharger: fresh air, open space, mountains or water.
D. Culture Learner: history, old streets, museums, traditions.
E. Food And Photo Traveller: local food, warm feeling, beautiful views.
Choose your main travel style.
Starter: My main travel style is because.
Which style is clearly not you?
Which style is your second choice?
Which style fits your friend or family member?
Which style fits your normal weekend?
Helpful expressions: My style is closest to.
My second choice is.
I am not really a traveller.
My friend is more than me.
Build Your Travel Profile.
Choose three words that fit your travel personality today.
calm / lively / organized / adventurous / comfortable / curious / social / independent / creative / practical / romantic / careful.
Choose three travel words for yourself.
Starter: My three words are,, and.
Which word is the most important?
Which word is not like you?
Which word describes your normal life too?
Which word describes only your vacation personality?
Helpful expressions: The most important word is.
I am usually.
On vacation, I become more.
I am not really.
Build Your Travel Profile.
Imagine one normal travel day.
What do you need to enjoy it?
Maybe you need a good cafe, clean streets, a quiet hotel, beautiful scenery, easy trains, good food, free time, or a place to practise English.
What do you need every day on a trip?
Starter: Every day on a trip, I need.
Do you need a slow morning?
Do you need one clear plan each day?
Do you need good food or coffee?
Do you need time alone?
Helpful expressions: I need a comfortable hotel.
I need good food.
I need time to rest.
I can enjoy a simple day.
Match Your Style To Places.
Switzerland may fit someone who likes clean cities, calm lakes, mountain views, trains, and peaceful travel.
It can feel organized and beautiful, but it is often expensive.
The Netherlands may fit someone who likes easy city life, canals, parks, bicycles, museums, and practical transport.
It can feel calm but still lively.
If you are a Calm Planner, which place fits?
Starter: For a calm trip, I would choose because.
Would you rather sit by a lake or walk beside a canal?
Does an organized place help you relax?
Is an expensive but calm trip worth it for you?
Which place sounds easier for a first trip?
Helpful expressions: It sounds peaceful.
It sounds easy to move around.
It may be too expensive for me.
I would check the cost first.
Match Your Style To Places.
Singapore may fit someone who likes clean city life, food courts, gardens, public transport, warm weather, and modern buildings.
South Korea may fit someone who likes cafes, shopping streets, music, city views, street food, and a mix of old and new culture.
If you are a City Explorer, which place fits?
Starter: For a city trip, I would choose because.
Do you like modern buildings and bright city views?
Would warm weather be good or difficult for you?
Do shopping streets give you energy or make you tired?
Which city sounds better for food?
Helpful expressions: I like modern cities.
I want easy public transport.
Busy streets can be exciting.
Busy streets can be tiring.
Match Your Style To Places.
New Zealand may fit someone who likes mountains, lakes, farms, hot springs, hiking, and open sky.
It can feel fresh and adventurous.
Canada may fit someone who likes big nature, forests, lakes, friendly city stops, and outdoor activities in different seasons.
If you are a Nature Recharger, which place fits?
Starter: For nature, I would choose because.
Would you rather see mountains, forests, lakes, or the sea?
Do you want a little adventure or a very easy trip?
Would a long flight change your answer?
Which season would you choose?
Helpful expressions: I want fresh air.
I like open space.
I would try a short hike.
A long flight might be difficult.
Match Your Style To Places.
Italy may fit someone who likes old cities, art, food, churches, small streets, and a strong feeling of history.
The Czech Republic may fit someone who likes castles, bridges, old town squares, music, warm food, and slow city walks.
If you are a Culture Learner, which place fits?
Starter: For culture and history, I would choose because.
Would you rather visit an art museum or a castle?
Do old streets make a place more interesting for you?
Do you like slow walking days?
What kind of history interests you?
Helpful expressions: I like old towns.
I enjoy places with history.
I want to walk slowly and look around.
Museums are interesting / not really my style.
Match Your Style To Places.
Greece may fit someone who likes blue sea, white houses, sunsets, cafes, simple food, and relaxed holiday feeling.
Thailand may fit someone who likes warm weather, street food, markets, beaches, friendly service, and colorful places.
If you are a Food And Photo Traveller, which place fits?
Starter: For food and photos, I would choose because.
Would you rather watch a sunset or walk through a market?
Do you enjoy trying new food?
Would very warm weather bother you?
Which place sounds better for a short trip?
Helpful expressions: I love sea views.
I want to try local food.
Warm weather is good for me.
Warm weather may be too much for me.
Choose And Explain Your Result.
Look back at your mood, travel style, three words, and daily needs.
Do not choose the most famous place.
Choose the place that matches you today.
What is your best match today?
Starter: Today my best match is because.
Which part helped you choose?
Does the result surprise you?
Which place is clearly not for you?
Would your result change in summer or winter?
Helpful expressions: My result makes sense because.
I was surprised because.
This place does not fit me because.
In winter, I might choose.
Choose And Explain Your Result.
Use this frame to make a clear answer.
My travel style is.
My best match is.
It fits me because.
My second match is.
Before a real trip, I would check.
Build your result sentence.
Starter: My travel style is, so my best match is.
Can you add one reason about feeling?
Can you add one reason about budget, weather, or transport?
What is your second match?
What should you check before a real trip?
Helpful expressions: The biggest reason is.
My practical reason is.
My second match is different because.
I would check first.
Choose And Explain Your Result.
Your answer is not fixed forever.
A different season, budget, travel partner, or mood can change the best match.
What could change your answer?
Starter: My answer could change if.
Would more money change your answer?
Would a family trip change your answer?
Would winter or summer change your answer?
Would better English confidence change your answer?
Helpful expressions: If I had more money, I might choose.
With my family, I would choose.
In summer, I prefer.
If my English improved, I might try.
Use It With Someone Else.
Now use the same idea for another person.
Ask about their personality first.
Then suggest a place and give one warning or check.
Suggest a place for a friend.
Starter: I think you should consider because you like.
What question would you ask your friend first?
What place would you not suggest?
What warning or advice would you give?
How can your friend check if the place is right?
Helpful expressions: First, I would ask.
I would not suggest because.
You should check the season.
You should check your budget and safety.
What feeling do you want on a trip?
On a free afternoon, what would you choose?
What can ruin a trip for you?
Choose your main travel style.
Choose three travel words for yourself.
What do you need every day on a trip?
If you are a Calm Planner, which place fits?
If you are a City Explorer, which place fits?
If you are a Nature Recharger, which place fits?
If you are a Culture Learner, which place fits?
If you are a Food And Photo Traveller, which place fits?
What is your best match today?
Build your result sentence.
What could change your answer?
Suggest a place for a friend.
A country does not have one personality.
A travel place has many sides.
This activity is not about finding a perfect answer.
It helps you describe yourself, compare choices, explain reasons, and give friendly advice.
